blocks.x: I just about run out of questions unless there's something special you want to add.
All in that, much more to say than what we have.
Yeah, well, I thought of some more. Wait a second. What are some of the little towns you played in in Mississippi and places like that?

Well, Mississippi, Paschristani, Gulfport, Biloxi, Paspergoula, Picayune, Poplarville, Lumberton, Addisburg, Electric Mill, Mississippi, Meridian. Electric Mill? Yeah. I never heard of that. Only everyone. Mm-hmm. That's Mississippi, Mobile, Alabama, Dresden, Alabama, Pensacola, Florida, Louisiana, that's right, Hazel Heights, Mississippi, McComb, Emmett, Louisiana, Hammond. Oh, that's enough.

You get the idea now, you played a whole lot of little towns. Yeah. What about this Red Book, Red Back Book? Did you ever play that, read out of that? Yeah, I have. You played those rags and everything, huh?
You mean those Red Book. Mm-hmm. What band was that?
Your own band or somebody else's? Own band.
In the South Wales and all those kind of numbers like that, bands, I don't know, they don't play those numbers anymore. Mm-hmm.
What are some of the different kind of jobs, you know, different places you played, like a picnic you say out at Millenburg, what are some of the other different things?
I played a lot of parades, parties, dance halls, night clubs. What else did people have in their homes? What other kind of parties and things?
Well, I played a lot of those paternity jobs up there.
I played big jobs up on Napoleon Avenue, St. Charles, the rich people, and out at West Bend, and so forth. Were they playing at fish fries?
No, I didn't play no fish fries. Never did. And what would they have with a fish fry?
Well at that time they would have a guitar player, one of those blues players, or after a graphing over, you know, records.
